branch_hypotheses.trigger: Lab evidence fails to support the pool link or points elsewhere.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Rising media attention to uncertainty itself, increased clinician complaints about ambiguity, and broader parent reliance on peer anecdotes over official statements.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Rumor networks gain agenda-setting power, clinicians become more frustrated, and the pool operator grows more defensive.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Lab results are delayed and official updates remain vague for multiple ticks.

branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Public attention shifts toward operational actions; parent sentiment splits between reassurance and suspicion.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: This may reduce some parent anxiety while also being interpreted by others as tacit admission of risk.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Pool operator voluntarily announces additional cleaning, temporary closure, or visible precaution before confirmation.

Media and community discourse repeatedly reference rumors as agenda-setting inputs.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Rumor correction is a stated focus and rumors are already active at T0.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional county health office has announced a cluster of stomach illness cases possibly linked to a public pool, with lab confirmation still pending. Parents are sharing rumors, pool staff fear reputational harm, clinicians want clear guidance, and county officials are trying to communicate uncertainty without overclaiming. T0 should preserve uncertainty and multiple credible paths including confirmation, false alarm, or delayed correction.

uncertainty_notes: Lab confirmation is pending at T0.
The public pool link is plausible but not established.
Institutional trust is relevant but not yet collapsed.

sociology_baseline.evidence: People are more likely to accept messages that fit prior caution or skepticism about local safety incidents.
Additional anecdotal cases or vivid posts could move more parents from observation to active warning behavior.
Some concerned individuals may stay quiet due to low certainty or job dependence.
Parent-to-parent and clinician-to-clinician sharing likely clusters by familiar networks.
Repeated exposure through peers and media may be needed before broader behavioral changes occur.
Role identities shape interpretation: caregiver protection, professional caution, and staff reputation defense.
Without confirming evidence or new developments, wider public attention may fade.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Official credibility depends on acknowledging uncertainty while still appearing competent and responsive.
Informal parent networks can spread warnings faster than formal channels, especially before lab results.
Pool-related actors have incentives to resist premature blame, shaping communication tone.
Ambiguous official language can create secondary uncertainty as clinicians improvise patient advice.
